change: in-app updater for the github release channel: two build flavours, automatic installs held until playback stops, and a release log rendered in the app

build_gate.lint: zero errors, abortOnError = true; 44 warnings, all pre-existing style and API-level advisories in the updater package
build_gate.note: release variants (:app:assembleGithubRelease, :app:assembleFdroidRelease, :app:lintRelease) are built by the release workflow, not by this local gate

covers: manifest parsing of untrusted documents: wrong types, unknown and duplicate ABIs, non-repository download addresses, oversized input
every trust refusal: foreign package, downgrade, replay, older version name, foreign certificate digest, low API level, missing architecture
downloaded APK checks: size, checksum, package, version code, single signer, signer equalling the installed app, native architectures
version-name ordering across the four-level policy
downloader against a local socket server: redirect following, monotonic progress, oversized response, connection dying mid-file

the two pacing rules (fifteen-minute floor for every request, six-hour interval for the app's own check, failed attempts never starting the interval, a corrected clock treated as expired), the minutes reported to the user, and banner dismissal hiding only the notice for that release, including the notice that an update waits for playback

the playback guard as a truth table: with automatic updates on, an install the app starts is refused while playing and refused on an unknown playback fact, and allowed only when stopped; with the setting off nothing installs unattended
the sequence the guard exists for: a night that begins in playback and ends when audio stops produces exactly one install, at the stop
the commit-time re-read of the playback guard: playback that starts during the APK copy abandons the installer session and never reaches the commit; a tap the owner made is not vetoed
the automatic request rule composed from the setting, the connection and both pacing intervals, including that a failed attempt never spends the six hours
resumption of a verified download after a process restart: only while that version is still newer and its file is still on disk

release notes present, absent (a schema-1 document with no log parses with an empty log and identical trust fields), and hostile (log that is not a list, entries and versions that are malformed, notes that are not strings, a newline in a date, repeated versions, 200 entries, a 2000-character line of control characters), each leaving the version, code, certificate and APK list identical to the clean parse and bounding what the view may draw
a declared schemaVersion newer than this build is read rather than refused

release_tools.note: includes the manifest generator's schema, URLs and rejection cases, the release log generated from a written changelog (bounded, de-duplicated versions, issue references stripped, a missing changelog publishing no notes) and the manifest refusing a log it cannot publish, the recipe's flavour selection per tag (asserting at least one tag was read), and the fdroid recipe block for new releases, plus the F-Droid channel asset the release job publishes beside the update options

pacing.every_request: at least fifteen minutes since the previous attempt, recorded before the request so a failed fetch or parse counts
pacing.app_initiated: at most once every six hours, measured from the last successful answer, so a failed attempt never spends that interval
pacing.user_initiated: gated by the fifteen-minute floor only

github.updater_code: present, the two new classes included, checked in both dex tables of the debug APK

fdroid.updater_code: none of the classes tools/check_release.py looks for appears in any dex: GithubUpdater, ReleaseFetch, ReleaseManifestParser, PackageInstalls, UpdateInstallReceiver, CheckThrottle, UpdatePrefs, InstallResults, Apks, UpdatePolicy, ReleaseManifest, UpdateState, UpdateApi, UpdateUi. The debug APK built by this change was also scanned for the two classes the release log and the install guard add, UpdateAutomation and UpdateLog, and carries neither. The whole app/src/github source set is excluded from this build, so the absence follows from the build graph as well as from this scan; the scan is what would catch a class drifting into shared code. Those two names are not yet in check_release.py's list, which another open change owns.

structure: every updater source file lives in app/src/github; app/src/main names no update type, calling three flavour-provided composables and handing one a Flow<Boolean> of play/pause instead; INTERNET appears only in app/src/github/AndroidManifest.xml
recipe: a build block may select the fdroid flavour only when the tag it pins defines the flavours; tools/check_release.py reads app/build.gradle.kts at each tag and android.yml now fetches tags so the rule is checked rather than skipped
not_verified: PackageInstaller install path on a device or emulator: this machine has no /dev/kvm
an unattended install: no install, no automatic restart and no post-install release-log view was observed
the waiting state, the install a play-to-pause transition triggers and the commit-time deferral; covered as rules, state transitions and an ordering test over a fake session, not observed
STATUS_PENDING_USER_ACTION confirmation dialog and the post-install restart
a download of a real published release from GitHub (tests use a local HTTP server)
behaviour behind captive portals, proxies or per-OEM installer prompts
the settings toggle, the waiting row and the release-log dialog rendered on a screen; compiled and linted only
the installer-outcome plumbing, the foreground reconciliation and the once-only release-log record: Android-bound, not unit-tested

automatic_updates.default: on in the github channel, stored in private preferences, switchable in Settings → Updates
automatic_updates.install_window: a downloaded, verified update becomes a ready-to-install state and is handed to PackageInstaller only when the setting is on and playback is known to be stopped; an unknown playback fact refuses, so a race postpones an install rather than interrupting audio
automatic_updates.user_initiated: a tap on Update installs without waiting, because the user asked
automatic_updates.pacing: unchanged: the fifteen-minute floor and the six-hour interval below still decide every request
automatic_updates.commit_time: the window is read once more immediately before the installer session commits, because copying the APK takes seconds with Play still live

release_log.shape: up to 8 releases, newest first, each {version, date, notes[0..4]}, each note at most 120 characters
release_log.generator: tools/package_release.py release_log() reads the CHANGELOG.md sections the release workflow has already written; no note is hand-authored
release_log.in_app: stored in private preferences and rendered from that copy, so the view makes no request of its own; shown once after an install this channel placed, and listed under Settings → Updates
